topic.title: Adaptive Online Learning and Prediction-Assisted Decisions
topic.overview: Online learning updates decisions as observations arrive, often without assuming a fixed data distribution. This topic studies regret guarantees, adaptation to easy or changing sequences, abstention, and use of predictions about future inputs. The learner must exploit helpful structure while retaining protection when that structure is absent or misleading.
topic.whyItMatters: Average performance against a fixed comparator may not capture changing needs or uneven consequences. Dynamic guarantees and confidence sequences provide other ways to assess repeated decisions. Computation also matters when each update requires an expensive optimization oracle rather than a simple parameter step.
topic.evolution: A 1996 analysis examines generalization during online training on finite samples. Later work develops implicit, parameter-free, and strongly adaptive methods. A 2024 classifier benefits from accurate future-example predictions without worsening worst-case regret; a 2026 resource-allocation framework combines online learning with uncertainty bounds for specified social-welfare objectives.
openQuestions: How can learners exploit predictable inputs while detecting deteriorating advice?
Which comparators reflect the practical cost of adapting after repeated changes?

papers.title: Avoiding Catastrophe in Online Learning by Asking for Help
papers.tldr: Under stated learnability and knowledge-transfer assumptions, mentor queries enable online learning with vanishing regret and a vanishing query rate despite catastrophic risk.

papers.title: Improved and Oracle-Efficient Online $\ell_1$-Multicalibration
papers.tldr: Direct optimization improves online l1 multicalibration rates, with a separate oracle-efficient method offering better scalability.

papers.title: Online Learning in the Random-Order Model
papers.tldr: A general adaptation makes stochastic online learners work in random order while largely preserving their regret guarantees.

papers.title: Online Linear Classification with Massart Noise
papers.tldr: An efficient online classifier reaches a qualitatively tight Massart-noise mistake bound and supports a bandit algorithm under linear reward-ranking assumptions.

papers.title: Provable Length Generalization in Sequence Prediction via Spectral Filtering
papers.tldr: A spectral-filtering algorithm provably generalizes in context length for linear dynamical systems under a new asymmetric regret measure.

papers.title: The Relationship Between No-Regret Learning and Online Conformal Prediction
papers.tldr: The paper identifies where standard regret fails to imply coverage and connects stronger online learning structure to adversarial and group-conditional conformal guarantees.

papers.title: Agnostic Continuous-Time Online Learning
papers.tldr: The paper characterizes how query budgets and hypothesis complexity govern regret when learning from continuous-time streams.

papers.title: Are Greedy Task Orderings Better Than Random in Continual Linear Regression?
papers.tldr: Greedy task ordering can accelerate learning empirically, but its theoretical behavior depends strongly on task rank and repetition.

papers.title: Consistency of the $k_n$-nearest neighbor rule under adaptive sampling
papers.tldr: Nearest-neighbor learning remains online consistent under adaptive sampling when a smoothing assumption and suitable neighbor-count choices hold.

papers.title: Online Portfolio Selection with ML Predictions
papers.tldr: RAM incorporates investment forecasts while providing separate wealth guarantees for perfect and adversarial predictions.

papers.title: Online Strategic Classification With Noise and Partial Feedback
papers.tldr: An online classifier achieves convergence and sublinear regret despite strategic feature manipulation, positive-only label feedback, and bounded feature-dependent noise.

papers.title: Prediction with expert advice under additive noise
papers.tldr: The paper derives sharp regret bounds showing how the distribution of additive feedback noise affects prediction with expert advice.

papers.title: Replicable Online Learning
papers.tldr: The paper develops online learners that achieve sublinear regret while reproducing the same action sequence with high probability across independently sampled runs.

papers.title: Tradeoffs between Mistakes and ERM Oracle Calls in Online and Transductive Online Learning
papers.tldr: Oracle-only online learning trades prediction quality against the number and type of optimization queries.

papers.title: Online Social Welfare Function-based Resource Allocation
papers.tldr: A general framework learns repeated resource allocations while providing anytime-valid welfare bounds across several social welfare objectives.

papers.title: The Cost of Learning Under Multiple Change Points
papers.tldr: Anytime Tracking CUSUM selectively responds to significant changes and achieves nearly minimax-optimal regret when properly tuned.
